exposure: cervical findings under flexible outpatient hysteroscopy (cervical stenosis, tortuous cervical canal)
abnormal sonographic findings (submucous myoma, endometrial polyp, endometrial hyperplasia)
abnormal hysteroscopic intracavitary findings (endometrial polyp, submucous myoma, intrauterine adhesions)
cohort: The study included 650 women undergoing their first in vitro fertilization (IVF)/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) cycles, with 605 proceeding to embryo transfer.
finding: Outpatient hysteroscopy (OH) can identify cervical characteristics, such as cervical stenosis or tortuous cervical canal, that are associated with a high incidence of difficult embryo transfer, with tortuous cervical canal showing a significantly higher incidence of difficult ET than cervical stenosis.
